gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Synology rates its own 2-bay DS225+ for only 10 Synology Drive users and 100,000 Drive-hosted files, while the 4-bay DS425+ with the same 2 GB of memory is rated for 20 users and 500,000 files. The cheapest Synology can fall short of a team moving years of Google Drive files, and the pick moves to the DS425+ or a UGREEN NASync.
standout_why: I compared against the three cited pages: the Synology Drive Technical Specifications page, the Drive Admin Console help and the Drive Quick Start Guide for administrators. I also checked the top uncited results (the Drive release notes, the QuickConnect pages and the DSM spec pages). The Drive spec page gives no per-model numbers; it says only that 'the recommended number of concurrent computer-client connections varies by Synology model' and points to each product page. None of these pages has a price or names a model. ChatGPT itself said only '4-bay Synology' with a guessed $1,000–1,500, and it priced Workspace at $12 a user a month, while Google's page today says $14 for Business Standard. Our current page has the DS225+ 10-user rating but not the 100,000-file cap. It also assumes about $250 of B2 over three years, which is too low at today's $6.95/TB rate.
decides: The cap changes which Synology to buy, not the yes-or-no answer. The DS223j (5 users, 100k files) and the DS225+ (10 users, 100k files) are both too tight for five people bringing an existing Drive archive. Synology's own figures put the 4-bay DS425+ (20 users, 500k files) or the DS925+ (80 users, 500k files) at the floor, which matches ChatGPT's '4-bay' advice and gives it a reason. On cost: 5 seats of Business Standard at $14 come to $2,520 over three years, against roughly $620 for a UGREEN DXP4800 Plus plus drives plus $250–500 of offsite backup on B2 (1–2 TB). Business Starter, at 5 × $7 × 36 = $1,260, only gives 30 GB pooled per user, so it is no real Drive replacement. For a remote team that edits files rather than chats in Docs, the NAS still wins on three-year cost.
